title: Neither Fizz nor Buzz
statement: How many of the integers $1, 2, \dots, 1000$ are divisible by neither $3$ nor $5$?
hints: Count the ones divisible by $3$ or by $5$ first. Which numbers did you count twice?
solution: There are $333$ multiples of $3$, $200$ of $5$ and $66$ of $15$. By inclusion–exclusion, $333+200-66 = 467$ are divisible by $3$ or $5$, leaving $1000-467 = 533$.
